status.detail: For an explicit --expire-at date/time that is already past, SetExpirableKeepAwake cancels existing state, logs an error, and returns before establishing an expirable state; the CLI does not surface a failure result. Preserve time-only rollover to the next day (#41205).

judgment.rationale: For an explicit --expire-at date/time that is already past, SetExpirableKeepAwake cancels existing state, logs an error, and returns before establishing an expirable state; the CLI does not surface a failure result. Preserve time-only rollover to the next day (#41205).
evidence: The issue gives an explicit past date/time and expects Awake to report expiry and exit.

title: [Awake] Awake should exit if a past expiry time is provided

fix_assessment.rationale: Source confirms an early-return path for past explicit expiry; a narrow CLI validation/error path is directly testable.

proposed_fixes.title: Reject expired absolute Awake CLI expiry values
proposed_fixes.root_cause: An absolute past expiry reaches SetExpirableKeepAwake, which cancels current state, logs, and returns without a clear CLI failure result.
plan: Distinguish time-only expiry from explicit date-and-time expiry during CLI parsing.
For an explicit absolute expiry at or before now, report an error and return nonzero before changing Awake mode.
Leave time-only expiry rollover-to-next-day behavior unchanged.
Add tests for past absolute, future absolute, past time-only, and malformed expiry values.
verification: Run with a past explicit date and verify error, nonzero exit, and no non-expiring Awake state.
Run --expire-at=00:00:00 after midnight and verify next-day scheduling remains intact.
Verify future explicit expiry still enters expirable mode.

confidence.rationale: The source early-return and reported absolute-date case align; tests isolate it from time-only rollover.

initial_investigation: Inspected Awake/Core/Manager.cs SetExpirableKeepAwake: CancelExistingThread precedes past-time check; branch logs and returns before scheduling.
Issue explicitly cross-references #41205 for time-only rollover; preserve that distinct behavior.
issue_context.analysis: Validate an explicit absolute timestamp before changing Awake state and return a CLI error; keep time-only rollover separate.
known_information: The report lists an absolute past timestamp and a time-only past value as separate cases.
For explicit past date/time the reporter expects a message and exit; time-only past should roll to tomorrow per #41205.
Manager.SetExpirableKeepAwake logs and returns when expireAt <= DateTimeOffset.Now after cancelling existing state.
inferences: The early return explains lack of explicit error result; exact resulting mode depends on caller/state lifecycle.
issue_context.summary: Awake CLI accepts an explicit past expiry timestamp, logs the condition in the manager, and returns without a clear failure result; the user expects the CLI to exit rather than leave non-expiring behavior.
